title: Power Rankings: Lakers, Bulls battle for top spot
heading: 2010-11 Power Rankings: Week 22
author: Marc Stein

rankings.summaryHtml: Only three times in the last 10 seasons has the team with the best record after the All-Star break won it all. The way that the reigning champs have been rolling, that amounts to a ray of hope for the rest of the field.

rankings.summaryHtml: Remember our recent suggestion in this cyberspace that the Bulls had to spruce up that pedestrian 15-13 road record? Check. They're 6-2 on the road since to help cement their status as the league's clear-cut No. 2.

rankings.summaryHtml: With seven of their nine games left against teams with losing records -- and knowing how clinical they are (32-5) against the sub-.500 set -- you can't completely dismiss the Heat's chances of snagging the East's top seed.

rankings.summaryHtml: One more time in case you haven't heard it: Friday's collapse against Charlotte marked the first time in Celts history that they fell to a team 10 or more games under .500 after leading by 10 or more to start the fourth.

rankings.summaryHtml: The COY ballot is officially impossible thanks to what the Nuggets have done (12-4) minus Melo. George Karl's work, pre- and post-trade ... who's been better? Can't conclusively say Thibodeau, Popovich, whoever.

rankings.summaryHtml: Don't think anyone in OKC will mind too much at 11-2 in March, but Durant is in the midst of his lowest-scoring month all season (25.1 ppg) and almost never gets mentioned in an MVP race he was widely tipped to win.

rankings.summaryHtml: This probably speaks more to the ongoing Boston funk and Miami's recent 5-6 stretch against .500-or-better teams, but Orlando actually has the East's second-best record since the All-Star break ... at a modest 11-5.

rankings.summaryHtml: Some decent trivia from Elias that I didn't see coming: Do you know what Gerald Wallace has in common with Tim Duncan, Chris Webber and Walt Frazier? All of them have five career 40-point games after Wallace's latest.

rankings.summaryHtml: The problem for the Hornets, even if they hang on to a playoff spot, is that they're going to see San Antonio without noted Spurs killer D-West ... or stay matched up with the Lakers. Which would probably be worse.

rankings.summaryHtml: Something tells me Philly, after feeling sneaky good about the potential Miami matchup in Round 1, wouldn't mind seeing the Heat move up to No. 2 after surrendering 71 points to LeBron and D-Wade on Friday night.

rankings.summaryHtml: Nash has quietly wrested the assist lead away from Rondo, but I grudgingly have to concede that the best efforts of Captain Canada, Grant Hill and the best sixth man no one talks about -- Marcin Gortat -- won't be enough.

rankings.summaryHtml: The "race" for No. 8 in the East in a nutshell: Losing nine of their first 11 games in March couldn't knock the Bobs out. Instead? Weekend wins over the Celtics and Knicks make them the "hot" team in this "race."
